themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints surged to 15 last week versus a 1.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 757% spike (z-score: 6.12)—suggesting a sudden sanitation service failure or widespread neglect across Midwood/Ocean Parkway this past week.
evidence: 15 street sweeping complaints last week vs. 1.8 weekly average (757% increase, z-score: 6.12)
Complaints concentrated in single recent week, indicating acute failure rather than chronic issue
High statistical significance suggests systemic rather than isolated problem
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if contractor pulled resources, equipment failed, or schedule changed
Interview residents on specific blocks where complaints clustered—are streets visibly dirtier than usual?

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaint Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 57 last week from a 13.2 weekly average—a 330% spike (z-score: 7.65)—suggesting either a major event, construction surge, or new noise source plaguing the district this past week.
evidence: 57 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 13.2 weekly baseline (330% increase, z-score: 7.65)
Spike is recent and acute, not a gradual trend
Noise complaints are the third-highest category overall (1,805 over 90 days), indicating chronic baseline
reporting_angles: Map the 57 complaints spatially—are they clustered near one venue, construction site, or transit hub?
Interview residents and local business owners about new late-night activity, bars, or events
Check 311 complaint detail for noise types: vehicle, music, construction, street vending?

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Distress
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked to 17 last week from a 4.4 weekly average—a 289% increase (z-score: 8.01)—indicating potential infrastructure failure or blockage affecting multiple properties across Midwood this past week.
evidence: 17 sewer complaints last week vs. 4.4 weekly average (289% increase, z-score: 8.01)
High z-score indicates statistically significant departure from normal pattern
Sewer issues are low-frequency baseline complaint, making sudden spike more alarming
reporting_angles: Contact DEP: are there known sewer breaks, backups, or maintenance work in the district?
Interview affected residents about backup symptoms and duration
Investigate if complaints cluster geographically—could indicate localized main line failure

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal complaints jumped to 134 two weeks ago from a 33.1 weekly average—a 304% spike (z-score: 5.38)—disrupting traffic flow and pedestrian safety across the district as of two weeks ago.
evidence: 134 traffic signal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 33.1 weekly average (304% increase, z-score: 5.38)
Traffic signal condition is already top-10 complaint category overall (518 over 90 days)
Spike indicates acute technical or electrical problem affecting multiple intersections
reporting_angles: Contact DOT: what signals failed and why? Power outage, software glitch, or aging equipment?
Document which intersections were most affected and for how long
Interview residents and drivers about congestion and safety incidents during the malfunction

themes_detail.label: Tree and Branch Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints spiked to 6 last week from a 1.0 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 7.07), and overgrown tree/branch complaints hit 8 three weeks ago versus 1.4 average (482% increase)—suggesting a seasonal hazard or storm damage requiring citywide tree assessment in Midwood.
evidence: Dead/dying tree complaints: 6 last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 7.07)
Overgrown tree/branch complaints: 8 three weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average (482% increase, z-score: 5.96)
Two related spikes suggest coordinated problem—possible storm damage, drought stress, or pest outbreak
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department: have recent storms or weather caused tree damage in the district?
Investigate if complaints cluster in specific neighborhoods or street blocks
Interview arborists about tree health: disease, pest infestation, or environmental stress?
